featured_reviews.name: Hemani Impex
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re looking for a masterclass in how to turn a simple X-ray into a 24-hour suspense thriller, then Shahbazkers Diagnostic Centre Pvt Ltd in Mumbai truly delivers.

My mother had a fall and was advised an X-ray for her wrist and hip. We were confidently told the reports would be ready by 5:00 pm and conveniently shared on WhatsApp. Efficient, right? Well… not quite.

After three polite follow-ups, each met with the reassuringly vague “it’s not ready yet, we’ll update you,” we finally received the reports the next day. Apparently, the doctor needed to review them—and unfortunately, wasn’t available. Because, of course, nothing says urgency like a diagnostic delay when a patient is waiting to begin treatment.

Thankfully, the reports turned out normal. But one can’t help wondering—what if they weren’t? Are patients expected to pause their recovery plans while the system catches up?

All said and done, if promptness, communication, and basic coordination are on your checklist, you might want to keep exploring your options. If not, and you enjoy a bit of unpredictability with your healthcare experience, this place might just surprise you—in more ways than one.

HbA1c Test: Purpose, Procedure, Normal Range & Results
May 26, 2026 - By Lupin Diagnostics
India has over 10.1 crore people living with diabetes. A daily finger-prick reading captures just one moment. The HbA1c test normal range tells a fuller story. This simple blood test reveals your average blood sugar over three months. Here is everything you need to know about it.
What Is the HbA1c Test and How Does It Work?
Glucose in your blood naturally sticks to haemoglobin, the protein inside red blood cells. The more sugar in your blood, the more gets attached. Since red blood cells live for roughly three months, the HbA1c test captures your average blood sugar level over that entire period.
This makes it far more reliable than a single fasting reading. A fasting test changes with your last meal or stress levels. Glycated haemoglobin, on the other hand, reflects steady patterns. Think of it as a three-month report card for your blood sugar.
Here is how it differs from routine glucose checks:
A fasting blood sugar test measures glucose at one point in time.
The HbA1c test shows a percentage reflecting 90-day glucose control.
